# Model and source

```{r model-meta, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
ui_pk <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2019_sildenafil_dog"))
ui_ivivc <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2019_sildenafil_dog_ivivc"))
ui_vitro <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kim_2019_sildenafil_invitro"))
cat("* Citation: ", ui_pk$reference, "\n", sep = "")
cat("* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics11060251>\n")
```

Kim et al. made one immediate-release (IR, 20 mg) and three sustained-release
(SR, 60 mg) sildenafil tablets whose release is slowed by increasing amounts of
HPMC (SRfast, SRmedium, SRslow). Sildenafil dissolves well at gastric pH and
poorly above pH 6, so in dogs the SR tablets showed reduced bioavailability and
secondary plasma peaks. The authors modelled this in S-ADAPT by separating
dissolution from absorption: drug leaves the tablet by dose-normalised
Michaelis-Menten kinetics multiplied by a time-varying dissolved fraction,
FDiss,total, that is near 1 in the stomach, near 0 in the small intestine,
about 0.12 in the colon, and 0 again at the end of the gut. They then
correlated the fitted in vivo maximum dissolution rates with the in vitro ones
(pH 1.2) to obtain a level-A in vitro-in vivo correlation (IVIVC).

The paper contributes three models, all of which are packaged:

| Model | What it is | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `Kim_2019_sildenafil_invitro` | In vitro Michaelis-Menten dissolution at pH 1.2 | Eq 1, Table 3 |
| `Kim_2019_sildenafil_dog` | Population PK model with fitted per-formulation in vivo Vmax | Eqs 2-11, Table 4 |
| `Kim_2019_sildenafil_dog_ivivc` | The same model with in vivo Vmax computed from the in vitro Vmax | Eq 13, Tables 3-4 |

# Population

Twelve male beagle dogs aged 14-18 months (Orient Bio, Korea) were fasted
overnight and given a single tablet with 30 mL water: IR 20 mg or one of the
three SR tablets at 60 mg, three dogs per formulation (Methods 2.4). Plasma was
sampled to 48 h and assayed by LC-MS/MS (LLOQ 5 ng/mL). Body weight is not
reported and is not used by the model.

```{r population, echo = FALSE}
str(ui_pk$population)
```

# Source trace

| Element | Value used | Source |
|---|---|---|
| In vitro dissolution ODE | `dX/dt = -Vmax * X / (AM50 + X)` (dose-normalised) | Eq 1; Methods 2.6.2 |
| In vitro AM50/dose | 0.395 (BSV 0.0316) | Table 3 |
| In vitro Vmax/dose IR, SRfast, SRmedium, SRslow | 6.58, 1.40, 0.358, 0.124 1/h | Table 3 |
| In vivo dissolution ODE | `dX/dt = -Vmax,in vivo * X / (AM50,in vivo + X) * FDiss,total` | Eq 2 (see Errata) |
| FDiss,total | FDiss,stomach + FDiss,intestine | Eq 3 |
| FDiss,stomach | `1 - Imax * t^H_s / (TGET^H_s + t^H_s)` | Eq 4 |
| FDiss,intestine | `Dissmax * t^H_i/(Ttrans1^H_i + t^H_i) * (1 - t^H_i/(Ttrans2^H_i + t^H_i))` | Eq 5 |
| Ttrans1, Ttrans2 | TGET + TITT; TGET + TITT + TCTT | Eqs 6-7 |
| Lumen, gut | `dXLumen/dt = diss - klag*XLumen`; `dXGut/dt = klag*XLumen - ka*XGut` | Eqs 8-9 |
| Disposition | two-compartment, CL and CLD | Eqs 10-11 |
| V1, V2 | 22 L (BSV 0.157), 31 L (BSV 0.751) | Table 4 |
| CL | 9.97 L/h (BSV 0.2) | Table 4, row printed as CLD (see Errata) |
| CLD | 49.2 L/h (BSV 0.379) | Table 4, row printed as CL (see Errata) |
| klag, ka | 3.13 1/h (0.497), 4.37 1/h (0.952) | Table 4 |
| TGET, Imax, Hillstomach | 0.73 h (0.385), 0.992 (0.0027), 16.7 (0.0316) | Table 4 |
| TITT, TCTT | 2.18 h (0.434), 4.1 h (0.11) | Table 4 |
| Dissmax, Hillintestine | 0.115 (0.359), 13.1 (0.0316) | Table 4 |
| In vivo AM50/dose | 0.315 (0.105) | Table 4 |
| In vivo Vmax/dose IR, SRfast, SRmedium, SRslow | 4.42 (0.416), 1.71 (0.145), 0.781 (0.295), 0.219 (0.255) 1/h | Table 4 |
| IVIVC correlation | `Vmax,in vivo/Dose = 2.1411 * (Vmax,in vitro/Dose)^0.4388 - 0.6346` | Eq 13 |
| BSV scale | omega^2 = BSV^2 (S-ADAPT exponential model, BSV = log-scale SD) | Methods 2.6.3 |
| Residual error | not reported; zero placeholder | -- |

# Shared simulation helpers

```{r helpers}
formulations <- tibble::tibble(
  treatment = factor(c("IR", "SRfast", "SRmedium", "SRslow"),
                     levels = c("IR", "SRfast", "SRmedium", "SRslow")),
  dose = c(20, 60, 60, 60),
  FORM_SILDENAFIL_SRFAST = c(0, 1, 0, 0),
  FORM_SILDENAFIL_SRMEDIUM = c(0, 0, 1, 0),
  FORM_SILDENAFIL_SRSLOW = c(0, 0, 0, 1)
)

# One subject per formulation (n_per_arm = 1) or n_per_arm subjects per
# formulation; dose into the tablet (depot), observe on a named ODE state.
make_events <- function(times, n_per_arm = 1, obs_cmt = "central") {
  subj <- formulations |>
    tidyr::uncount(n_per_arm) |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number())
  dose_rows <- subj |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose, cmt = "depot")
  obs_rows <- subj |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = obs_cmt)
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
    as.data.frame()
}

times_fine <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.05), 36, 48)))
ev_typ <- make_events(times_fine)

# Typical-value solve. The two muffled warnings are the expected notices for a
# zeroRe() model solved for several subjects (no omega, no sigma); any other
# warning still surfaces.
expected_typ_warning <- "multi-subject simulation without|No sigma parameters"
muffle_expected <- function(w) {
  if (grepl(expected_typ_warning, conditionMessage(w))) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
}
solve_typ <- function(ui, ev) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(ui), events = ev,
                    keep = c("treatment", "dose"),
                    returnType = "data.frame"),
    warning = muffle_expected
  )
}
```

# In vitro dissolution (Equation 1, Table 3)

```{r invitro}
ev_vitro <- make_events(seq(0, 24, by = 0.01), obs_cmt = "released")
sim_vitro <- solve_typ(ui_vitro, ev_vitro) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_released = 100 * released / dose)

ggplot(sim_vitro |> dplyr::filter(time <= 12),
       aes(time, pct_released, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Released (%)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Typical in vitro dissolution at pH 1.2",
       caption = "Replicates the pH 1.2 curves of Figure 2 and Figure S1 of Kim 2019.")

# Results 3.1: IR release 'completed within 0.4 h' at pH 1.2.
ir_04 <- sim_vitro$pct_released[sim_vitro$treatment == "IR" & abs(sim_vitro$time - 0.4) < 1e-9]
ir_04
stopifnot(ir_04 > 95)
# Release order IR > SRfast > SRmedium > SRslow at every time (Results 3.1).
ord <- sim_vitro |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8)) |>
  dplyr::select(time, treatment, pct_released) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = pct_released)
stopifnot(all(ord$IR > ord$SRfast), all(ord$SRfast > ord$SRmedium),
          all(ord$SRmedium > ord$SRslow))
```

# Time-varying dissolved fraction (Figure 4A)

FDiss,total is a deterministic function of time after dose and the typical
parameters, so the Results 3.3.2 statements can be checked exactly.

```{r fdiss}
sim_pk <- solve_typ(ui_pk, ev_typ)

fd <- sim_pk |>
  dplyr::filter(treatment == "IR", time <= 12) |>
  dplyr::select(time, fdiss_stomach, fdiss_intestine, fdiss_total) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-time)

ggplot(fd, aes(time, value, linetype = name)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Dissolved fraction", linetype = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4A of Kim 2019.")

fd_at <- function(t) sim_pk$fdiss_total[sim_pk$treatment == "IR" & abs(sim_pk$time - t) < 1e-9]
fd_min <- min(sim_pk$fdiss_total[sim_pk$treatment == "IR" & sim_pk$time >= 1 & sim_pk$time <= 2])
c(t0.25 = fd_at(0.25), t1 = fd_at(1), min_1_to_2h = fd_min, t3.2 = fd_at(3.2),
  t5 = fd_at(5), t6.3 = fd_at(6.3), t10 = fd_at(10))
stopifnot(
  fd_at(0.25) > 0.99,                    # 'estimated to be 100% until approximately 30 min'
  # 'decreased to the minimum fraction of 0.8% at 1 h': the floor is
  # 1 - Imax = 0.008, reached between 1 and 2 h (0.013 at exactly 1 h).
  fd_at(1) < 0.02, abs(fd_min - 0.008) < 0.001,
  fd_at(5) > 0.10,                       # 'remained above 10% within 3.2-6.3 h'
  abs(fd_at(3.2) - 0.10) < 0.02,         # window edges sit at about 10%
  abs(fd_at(6.3) - 0.10) < 0.02,
  fd_at(10) < 0.02                       # 'reached the minimum again at around 10 h'
)
```

# In vivo dissolution (Figure 4B)

```{r invivo-diss}
sim_ivivc <- solve_typ(ui_ivivc, ev_typ)
diss <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_pk |> dplyr::mutate(model = "Population PK (Table 4 Vmax)"),
  sim_ivivc |> dplyr::mutate(model = "IVIVC (Eq 13 Vmax)")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_dissolved = 100 * (1 - depot / dose))

ggplot(diss |> dplyr::filter(time <= 12),
       aes(time, pct_dissolved, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~model) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "In vivo dissolution (%)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 4B of Kim 2019.")

diss_tab <- diss |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(1, 12)) |>
  dplyr::select(model, treatment, time, pct_dissolved) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = time, values_from = pct_dissolved,
                     names_prefix = "t")
diss_tab |>
  dplyr::rename("Model" = model, "Tablet" = treatment,
                "Dissolved at 1 h (%)" = t1, "Dissolved at 12 h (%)" = t12) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

# Results 3.3.2: at 12 h SRmedium 63% and SRslow 21% dissolved; IR and SRfast
# almost complete.
d12 <- function(m, f) diss_tab$t12[diss_tab$model == m & diss_tab$treatment == f]
for (m in unique(diss_tab$model)) {
  stopifnot(
    abs(d12(m, "SRmedium") - 63) < 6,
    abs(d12(m, "SRslow") - 21) < 2,
    d12(m, "IR") > 99, d12(m, "SRfast") > 95
  )
}
```

# Systemic clearance: the printed Table 4 rows are transposed

The IR tablet dissolves completely (Figure 4B and above), so its
AUC(0-inf) equals Dose / CL regardless of the dissolution and absorption
details. The observed IR AUCinf is 2007 ng*h/mL (Table 2) and the paper's own
IVIVC prediction of AUCall is 1942 ng*h/mL (Table 5).

```{r cl-swap}
auc_from_cl <- function(cl) 20 * 1000 / cl   # ng*h/mL for 20 mg
c(printed_CL_49.2 = auc_from_cl(49.2), swapped_CL_9.97 = auc_from_cl(9.97),
  observed_Table2 = 2007.1)
stopifnot(abs(auc_from_cl(9.97) / 2007.1 - 1) < 0.02,
          auc_from_cl(49.2) / 2007.1 < 0.25)

# The packaged model gives the same AUC numerically (IR dissolves fully).
ir <- sim_pk |> dplyr::filter(treatment == "IR")
# AUC(0-48 h); the typical concentration at 48 h is below 0.1 ng/mL, so the
# remaining tail is negligible against the 2% bound.
auc_ir <- sum(diff(ir$time) * (head(ir$Cc, -1) + tail(ir$Cc, -1)) / 2)
c(model_AUC_0_48 = auc_ir, C48 = tail(ir$Cc, 1))
stopifnot(tail(ir$Cc, 1) < 0.1)
stopifnot(abs(auc_ir / auc_from_cl(9.97) - 1) < 0.02)

# The distribution clearance is then pinned by Cmax: with CLD = 49.2 L/h the
# typical IR Cmax is close to the Table 5 prediction (338.7 ng/mL); with
# CLD = 9.97 L/h as well it would be about 500 ng/mL.
alt <- solve_typ(ui_pk |> rxode2::ini(lq = log(9.97)), ev_typ)
c(model_Cmax = max(ir$Cc),
  CLD_9.97_Cmax = max(alt$Cc[alt$treatment == "IR"]))
stopifnot(abs(max(ir$Cc) / 338.7 - 1) < 0.1,
          max(alt$Cc[alt$treatment == "IR"]) / 338.7 > 1.3)
```

# Typical profiles and PKNCA against Tables 2 and 5

Table 5 compares the IVIVC-predicted mean Cmax and AUCall with the observed
values. The observed AUCall runs to the last quantifiable sample, which the
Table 2 AUCinf - AUCall difference and the reported half-lives place at 24 h
for IR, SRfast and SRmedium and at 12 h for SRslow (Figure 3), so the
simulated AUC uses those end times.

```{r pknca}
conc_typ <- sim_ivivc |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = as.integer(treatment)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
conc_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  conc_typ,
  conc_typ |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::arrange(treatment, id, time)

dose_typ <- formulations |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = as.integer(treatment), time = 0, amt = dose) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

intervals <- data.frame(
  treatment = formulations$treatment,
  start = 0,
  end = c(24, 24, 24, 12),
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
)

nca_typ <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_typ, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_typ, amt ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = intervals
))

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~auclast,
  "IR",        338.7, 1942.2,
  "SRfast",    797.4, 5609.2,
  "SRmedium",  439.9, 3896.7,
  "SRslow",    137.2, 1010.0
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_typ,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("cmax", "auclast"),
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", auclast = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = paste(
  "Typical-value IVIVC simulation vs the Kim 2019 Table 5 IVIVC predictions",
  "(Monte Carlo means). AUC is AUC(0-24 h), or AUC(0-12 h) for SRslow.",
  "* marks a difference greater than 20%."
))

sim_res <- as.data.frame(nca_typ) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")) |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = as.character(treatment)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(published, by = "treatment", suffix = c("_sim", "_pub"))
pct <- with(sim_res, c(100 * (cmax_sim / cmax_pub - 1), 100 * (auclast_sim / auclast_pub - 1)))
round(pct, 1)
# Deterministic typical-value solve against the paper's Monte Carlo means:
# both sides are fixed numbers, so a fixed bound is reproducible.
stopifnot(all(abs(pct) < 15), abs(median(pct)) < 8)
```

The fitted population PK model (Table 4 in vivo Vmax) and the IVIVC model
give typical profiles that differ only through the four in vivo Vmax values:

```{r typical-profiles}
prof <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  sim_pk |> dplyr::mutate(model = "Population PK"),
  sim_ivivc |> dplyr::mutate(model = "IVIVC")
)
ggplot(prof |> dplyr::filter(time <= 24),
       aes(time, Cc, colour = treatment, linetype = model)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Sildenafil (ng/mL)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
       caption = "Typical-value profiles; compare with Figure 3 of Kim 2019.")
```

# Stochastic prediction (Figure 6)

```{r vpc}
set.seed(2019)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2019)
ev_vpc <- make_events(c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 3.5, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8,
                        10, 12, 16, 20, 24), n_per_arm = 200)
sim_vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(ui_ivivc, events = ev_vpc, keep = "treatment",
                           returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim_vpc$Cc))

vpc <- sim_vpc |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p10 = quantile(Cc, 0.10), p25 = quantile(Cc, 0.25), p50 = median(Cc),
    p75 = quantile(Cc, 0.75), p90 = quantile(Cc, 0.90), .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p25, ymax = p75), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~treatment, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Sildenafil (ng/mL)",
       caption = paste("200 virtual dogs per tablet; median, 25-75th and",
                       "10-90th percentiles. Replicates Figure 6 of Kim 2019."))

# Medians of the plateau / peak region read from Figure 6 are of the order of
# 300 (IR, 1 h), 700 (SRfast, 1.5 h), 300 (SRmedium, 3 h) and 100 (SRslow, 4 h)
# ng/mL. Gate the median (centre of the cohort), not the tails.
med_at <- function(f, t) vpc$p50[vpc$treatment == f & vpc$time == t]
stopifnot(
  med_at("IR", 1) > 150, med_at("IR", 1) < 500,
  med_at("SRfast", 1.5) > 400, med_at("SRfast", 1.5) < 1100,
  med_at("SRmedium", 3) > 150, med_at("SRmedium", 3) < 500,
  med_at("SRslow", 4) > 50, med_at("SRslow", 4) < 160
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Table 4 CL and CLD rows are transposed.** The table prints systemic
  clearance CL = 49.2 L/h (BSV 0.379) and distribution clearance CLD =
  9.97 L/h (BSV 0.2). The IR tablet dissolves completely, so its AUC equals
  Dose / CL exactly; CL = 49.2 L/h gives 406 ng*h/mL, a fifth of the observed
  2007 ng*h/mL and of the paper's own IVIVC prediction (Table 5), while
  CL = 9.97 L/h gives 2006 ng*h/mL and matches the NCA CL/F of the IR and
  SRfast tablets (Table 2: 12.1 and 10.4 L/h). With CL = 9.97 L/h, only
  CLD = 49.2 L/h reproduces the Table 5 Cmax values. The packaged models
  swap the two rows, value and BSV together; which BSV belongs to which
  clearance cannot be checked independently.
* **Equation subscripts.** Equations (2) and (8) print the in vitro symbols
  Vmax,in vitro and AM50,in vitro in the rate term and FDiss,in vivo in
  Equation (8); the surrounding text defines Vmax,in vivo and AM50,in vivo as
  the parameters of the in vivo dissolution and FDiss,total as the
  multiplier, and Table 4 reports them. The models use the in vivo
  parameters and FDiss,total in both equations, so the amount leaving the
  tablet enters the lumen (mass balance).
* **Dose normalisation.** Methods 2.6.3 states that the tablet amount was
  normalised by the dose and that Vmax/dose and AM50/dose were estimated.
  The models write Equation (2) in amounts as
  `Vmax * X / (AM50 + X / Dose)` with `Dose = podo(depot)`. This reading
  reproduces the 63% (SRmedium) and 21% (SRslow) dissolved at 12 h stated in
  Results 3.3.2. The models are single-dose models: FDiss,total is a function
  of the time since the latest tablet, so overlapping tablets (repeated
  dosing before the previous tablet has left the colon) are not described.
* **Between-subject variability scale.** Table 4 does not state the scale of
  its BSV column. S-ADAPT reports BSV as the standard deviation of the
  log-scale random effect ('apparent CV'), so omega^2 = BSV^2. The 0.0316
  entries (Hill coefficients, in vitro AM50) equal sqrt(0.001), the usual
  small-variance floor of S-ADAPT fits, which supports this reading. They
  are not marked as fixed in the paper and are not fixed here.
* **Imax variability.** Imax (0.992) carries an exponential random effect
  (BSV 0.0027), as stated for all parameters, so an individual Imax can
  slightly exceed 1 (by at most about 0.01 at 3 SD), giving a marginally
  negative FDiss,stomach after gastric emptying. The effect on dissolution is
  negligible and the model is kept as published.
* **Residual error.** No residual-error model or estimate is reported. The
  models carry a proportional residual SD fixed to zero as a placeholder;
  the in vitro model has no observation error at all.
* **IVIVC variability.** The paper does not say which between-subject
  variability its IVIVC Monte Carlo simulations (Section 2.7) applied to the
  correlated in vivo Vmax. `Kim_2019_sildenafil_dog_ivivc` applies the
  Table 4 per-formulation BSV of the fitted in vivo Vmax to the correlated
  value. The in vitro Vmax inputs and the Equation (13) coefficients are
  fixed: they come from separate fits (Table 3 and the SigmaPlot
  regression). Equation (13) returns a non-positive in vivo rate for in vitro
  Vmax/dose below about 0.062 1/h, outside the 0.124-6.58 1/h range on which it
  was built.
* **Figure 4B.** The Figure 4B curves match the IVIVC-derived in vivo Vmax
  (SRmedium 63% at 12 h, 38% at 1 h) slightly better than the Table 4 fitted
  values (67% and 41%); both are within the tolerance used above.
* **In vitro dissolution at pH 4.5 and 6.8** (Figure 2) was not modelled by the
  authors and is not represented.
* **Body weight** is not reported; doses are flat tablet amounts.
